chunks: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام used to say:

Whoever frequently goes to the mosques attains one of eight things: a brother beneficial in Allah, or newly acquired knowledge, or a definitive verse, or an awaited mercy, or a word that turns him back from ruin, or he hears a word that guides him to guidance, or he leaves a sin out of fear, or out of modesty.

key_terms.آيَةً مُحْكَمَةً: a definitive verse, a clear and firm sign or revealed teaching
key_terms.أَخًا: a brother, meaning a beneficial companion in faith
key_terms.الْمَسَاجِدِ: the mosques, places of worship and communal spiritual benefit
key_terms.ذَنْبًا: a sin, an act of disobedience left behind
key_terms.رَحْمَةً: mercy, divine favor and spiritual blessing
key_terms.هُدًى: guidance, direction toward what is right

ai.seo_question: What benefits does Imam Ali عليه السلام mention for frequently attending the mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the spiritual, moral, and social benefits of frequenting the mosques. It presents the mosque as a place of beneficial companionship, knowledge, guidance, mercy, and moral reform. The saying encourages regular attendance by showing that it nurtures both worship and character.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.713 - The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) used to say:

"Whoever frequently visits the mosques will attain one of eight benefits: a brother (friend) beneficial in the cause of Allah (swt), newly acquired knowledge, a definitive verse (of guidance), a mercy awaited, a word that turns him away from misguidance, hearing a word that leads him to guidance, abandoning a sin out of fear (of Allah (swt)) or out of shame”.
